newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends bourse at record closing high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends bourse at record closing high.

text.p: The German DAX index ended bourse dealings at an all-time record closing high on Wednesday, continuing a rally started in Tuesday's post-bourse electronic trade after the dollar recovered against the mark.
The DAX index finished floor dealings up 39.13 points, or 1.43 percent, at a record bourse close of 2,773.43 points, off an intraday high of 2,775.96 points reached in in late bourse trade.
"The lights are all on green," said one trader.
Dealers said a record close on Wall Street, strength on the DAX future contract and surprisingly good nine month results from utility giant Veba had all helped feed the rally.
Tuesday's late IBIS climb had come after comments by Bundesbank council member Edgar Meister that the dollar trading below 1.50 marks was "not appropriate", boosted the U.S. currency.
Bourse dealings, particularly in export-oriented chemicals and carmaker shares, had been held back on Tuesday as the dollar traded at a two-month low near 1.49 marks.

The dollar got another boost after the Tuesday IBIS close on comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that the dollar was once again on its way higher and that he always welcomed the dollar being at its correct level.
After Tietmeyer's comments the dollar pulled above the crucial 1.50 mark level and on Wednesday climbed further to stablise around 1.5060 marks, further encouraging German stocks.
But dealers said they saw momentum lessening. "The rally is feeding the rally, but today with somewhat less foaming at the mouth," said one dealer.

From a chart technical point of view, traders said the market was showing signs of being overbought and could enter a phase of consolidation ahead of the market turbulence expected next week when shares in national telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom are floated.
Whether the DAX index can reach the technical and psychological level of 2,800 points this week would depend on the performance of the dollar and Wall Street, dealers said.
Veba surprised the market by reporting a 25 percent climb in nine month net profit to 1,227 billion marks.

Meanwhile nine month figures releases by chemicals and drugs group BASF AG were somewhat disappointing, dealers said, and the stock ended bourse dealings weaker than the market, but still up 21 pfennigs at 51.55 marks.
Diversified industrial giant Daimler Benz AG reached a year-high of 98.10 marks, before paring gains to end bourse trade up 3.70 marks at 97.85 marks.
Dealers said that as a major exporter Daimler had benefited in particular from the dollar recovery and said some investment houses had also repeated earlier buy recommendations on the stock.
